cards.title: Already paid or shared details?
cards.body: Act quickly. Open 'Already paid?' in Ruko for the official helplines and the steps to take, in order.

cards.title: Who is this payment going to?
cards.body: SEBI-registered brokers and other intermediaries must use special UPI IDs ending in '@valid' plus the bank's name to collect UPI payments. A personal UPI ID, phone number or bank account shared in a chat is something else. You can check a UPI ID yourself on SEBI Check (link below).

sources.source_title: SEBI circular SEBI/HO/DEPA-II/DEPA-II_SRG/P/CIR/2025/86: Adoption of Standardised, Validated and Exclusive UPI IDs for Payment Collection by SEBI Registered Intermediaries from Investors

lessons.title: Why promised returns matter
lessons.body: SEBI's guide to spotting scams says to be suspicious of anyone who promises assured or near-certain returns, because all securities market investments carry some degree of risk. SEBI's investor website also says registered investment advisers are prohibited from guaranteeing returns. When a message promises a fixed or daily return, the promise itself is what to look at, not the sender's story. Ruko can't vouch for any tip, app or person.

terms.title: SEBI
terms.brief: The Securities and Exchange Board of India, the regulator of India's securities market.

terms.title: Emergency money
terms.brief: Money kept aside for sudden needs such as a medical bill or a lost job, separate from money meant for investing.

terms.title: Share (stock)
terms.brief: A small part-ownership of a company. Its price on the exchange moves as buyers and sellers agree on new prices.

terms.title: F&O (futures and options)
terms.brief: Contracts whose value depends on a share or an index. A small price move can change your rupees by a lot compared with the money put in.

terms.title: IPO (initial public offering)
terms.brief: A company's first sale of shares to the public. You apply during a window, and applying does not mean you will get shares.

terms.title: Mutual fund
terms.brief: A pool of many people's money, run by a fund manager, that holds shares, bonds or both. You own units of the pool.
